paper.title: WRN structural flexibility showcased through fragment-based lead discovery of inhibitors

extraction.notes: Three assay blocks taken from the Methods subsections. Tags and exact residue ranges per assay are in Supporting Table SI 1, which was not fetched.

substrate.description: ATP, added at 1x Km to initiate the reaction

supplier.name: all black NBS low-volume 384 well microplates

top_concentration.verbatim: three-fold serial dilution (100 µM, the Top highest concentration)

positive.name: positive inhibition control (concentration as printed; 20 mM is implausible for an inhibitor control and the sister paper on the same assay states 20 µM)

concentration.verbatim: WRN + Substrates + 20 mM positive inhibition control

controls.normalisation: High luminescence (enzyme + substrates + DMSO) represents the signal from max ATP hydrolysis (no ATPase inhibition), while low luminescence ... represents no ATPase activity/complete inhibition.

interference_and_counterscreens.notes: The same ATPase format was run against BLM helicase core (642–1296) as the selectivity counterscreen. ADP-Glo is a luciferase-coupled readout, so luciferase interference applies.

analysis.fit_model: 4-parameter (4P) inhibition model, giving IC50, Hill slope and % maximum inhibition

evidence.quote: To measure WRN ATPase activity, the accumulation of ADP was quantitated via ADP-Glo Assay kit (Promega) in all black NBS low-volume 384 well microplates (Corning, 3820).
All assay reaction solutions were prepared in 1X assay buffer (25 mM HEPES-NaOH, pH 7.3, 50 mM NaCl, 2 mM MgCl2, 0.01% Tween-20, 0.5 mM TCEP, 1% DMSO).
assembled in a final volume of 20 µL by preincubating (250 pM, final) WRN helicase core (500–942) with the respective compound
for 30 min in the presence of (100 nM, final) single stranded DNA ... which is required for ATP hydrolysis, prior to reaction initiation by the 1:1 addition of 1X Km ATP (50 µM, final)
Both BLM and WRN ATPase reactions were run for 1 h prior to quenching by the addition of the ADP-Glo kit reagents.

The helicase domain of Human Werner-Syndrome (WRN) protein UniProt ID Q14191 for SPR, X-ray, biochemistry, and bioNMR was expressed using the residues and tags as described in the Supporting Table SI 1.

target.construct_verbatim: N-terminal GST-PRE and C-terminal AVI-tagged human WRN (500–946) was cloned into pFastBac1

concentration.verbatim: A solution of 100 μg/mL WRN ... was injected into flow cell 2 ... to achieve an immobilization density of ~3000 RU

plate.coating: Series S CAP sensor chip, biotin capture (Biotin Capture Kit, Cytiva)

supplier.name: Series S CAP Sensor chip / Biotin Capture Kit

stock.verbatim: compound stocks of 100 mM in 100% DMSO were diluted 100-fold in assay buffer

top_concentration.verbatim: 4 concentration points for each fragment samples including 125 μM, 250 μM, 500 μM and 1000 μM

screening_campaign.library_name: internal non-fluorine containing fragment collection (diversity set)

screen_concentration.verbatim: diluted 100-fold in assay buffer to a 1 mM final test concentration with 1% DMSO

screening_campaign.hit_criterion: binding occupancy vs the 1:1 theoretical maximum; hits with less than 20% occupancy were deprioritized, then clustered by kinetic profile and only ranks 1 and 2 progressed
cascade: SPR Tier 2 dose-response (4 concentrations, top 1 mM)

negative: flow cell 1 reserved as the reference cell for reference cell correction
controls.normalisation: Binding occupancy for each test fragment was calculated using the ratio of observed binding RU (at the end of each test fragment injection) and the theoretical maximum occupancy based on a 1:1 binding model.

interference_and_counterscreens.notes: A DMSO solvent correction was applied for refractive-index mismatch, using a standard curve of five concentrations in 0.5% steps from 0% to 2% DMSO. This is an instrument artefact correction, NOT a DMSO tolerance experiment, so quality.dmso_tolerance_tested_pct is deliberately left empty.

evidence.quote: The SPR binding assays were carried out using a high-throughput Biacore 8 K + SPR system (Cytiva), with biotinylated WRN protein immobilized to the biosensor chip surface using a proprietary biotin capture method (Biotin Capture Kit; Cytiva).
The sensor chip was subsequently equilibrated at 20 °C in running buffer (10 mM HEPES-NaOH, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% Tween 20, 1% DMSO) prior to analysis of test compounds.
The diversity set of 500 fragments from our internal non-fluorine containing collection was subjected to a series of SPR binding assays.
For SPR measurements, the N-terminal GST-PRE and C-terminal AVI-tagged human WRN (500–946) was cloned into pFastBac1.

readers.name: AVANCE III 600 MHz NMR spectrometer with 5 mm QCI-F cryoprobe

instrumentation.read_mode: 19F CPMG T2 relaxation, 20 ms and 160 ms total relaxation time, 112 scans, proton decoupling

screening_campaign.library_name: internal fluorine-containing fragment collection, pooled in mixtures of up to 21 compounds
screening_campaign.hit_criterion: signal intensity change with Qbind < 0.5, then singleton confirmation by 1H T2 CPMG, STD and waterLOGSY

negative: control samples of each mixture component without protein
compound QC samples at 200 uM in buffer with 2.5% DMSO-d6
controls.normalisation: peak intensities in the presence of protein compared with reference spectra for the individual compounds in buffer

interference_and_counterscreens.notes: Fragments were pre-selected for purity >90%, solubility >250 uM and lack of aggregation at 50 uM in CPMG experiments.

evidence.quote: The 1020 fragments from internal fluorine-containing collection were selected based on their measured 19F chemical shifts, purity >90%, solubility >250 µM, and lack of aggregation at 50 µM in the CPMG experiments.

Samples to evaluate binding were prepared in 25 mM HEPES-NaOH, 50 mM NaCl, 2 mM MgCl2, pH 7.4 buffer with protein concentration at 10 µM and each mixture component at 50 µM, with DMSO-D6 concentration matched to 2.5% final volume in each sample.
The 19F CPMG relaxation experiments were recorded at 295 K on a Bruker AVANCE III 600 MHz NMR spectrometer equipped with a 5 mm QCI-F cryoprobe.
